mine: the region of Geliloth near the Jordan
note: Geliloth hayyarden may be a common noun "circuits, districts" (KJV) or the place name Geliloth (cf. 18:17); either is defensible.

kjv: at the passage of the children of Israel
mine: on the side belonging to the people of Israel
note: 'El-'ever bene yisra'el is "toward the side (region across) of the Israelites", locating the altar on the western, Israelite bank, which is why it caused offence; "passage" suggests a ford.
'El 'Elohim YHWH is a triple divine name; the KJV reads it as a construct "God of gods", which the grammar (no construct form) does not require.
Minchah here is the grain (cereal) offering; "meat" in 1611 meant food in general, but modern readers will think of flesh.

kjv: called the altar [Ed:] for it [shall be] a witness
mine: gave the altar a name: "It is a witness
note: The MT gives no name after "called the altar"; the KJV supplies "Ed" ("witness") in italics, following a few Hebrew MSS and the Syriac. I translate the MT, taking the following clause as the name.
